A Phase 3 study,
three things to know.

A summary of what this study is testing, who it's for, and how it differs from many clinical trials in CIDP and neurology.

PHASE 3

WHAT'S BEING TESTED

KIg10: an investigational IVIG 10% therapy

An intravenous immune globulin product is being tested as a maintenance therapy for adults with confirmed CIDP at two dose strengths.

  • Two dose groups: 0.5 g/kg and 1.0 g/kg, randomly assigned in a 1:2 ratio
  • A loading dose, then infusions every 3 weeks for 21 weeks
  • Both doses are active medication, with no placebo (double-blind study)
  • Total participation: approximately 8 to 10 months
ADULTS

WHO IT'S FOR

Adults with confirmed CIDP, currently on treatment

For adults whose CIDP has been treated with IVIG, SCIG, corticosteroids, or another standard therapy, and has remained stable in recent months.

  • Ages 18 and older
  • Diagnosed by a neurologist (EAN/PNS 2021)
  • Currently on CIDP treatment
  • Stable for at least 12 weeks

Important: every participant receives active medication.

Unlike many clinical studies, this Phase 3 trial does not use a placebo. Participants whose CIDP worsens during the wash-out phase are randomly placed in one of two dose groups: 0.5 g/kg or 1.0 g/kg of KIg10. The assignment is 1:2, meaning twice as many participants are placed in the 1.0 g/kg group. Both doses are active IVIG. The 1.0 g/kg dose is the currently recommended maintenance dose for CIDP, and the 0.5 g/kg dose is a lower dose. Everyone who starts treatment first receives a single loading dose of KIg10 (2.0 g/kg). Because this is a double-blind study, neither you nor the doctor will know which of the two doses you received, but every dose you receive in the treatment phase is active KIg10. If your CIDP worsens or does not improve during treatment, you switch to a higher dose of KIg10 (2.0 g/kg) every 3 weeks for the rest of the treatment phase.

Important Disclosure

Before the study medicine begins, your current CIDP treatment is gradually stopped.

This is the most important thing to understand about the study. Before randomization, all participants enter a wash-out phase of up to 12 weeks, This is the most important thing to understand about the study. Before randomization, all participants enter a wash-out phase of up to 12 weeks, during which your current IVIG or other CIDP treatment is gradually reduced and then stopped. This gives the study team a clean starting point to measure how KIg10 affects your condition.

Your symptoms are monitored closely, with study visits every 3 weeks and phone check-ins after each dose reduction. If your CIDP shows signs of worsening, specifically a change of 1 or more points on the INCAT disability score (a standard CIDP severity measure used by neurologists), the wash-out phase ends and study treatment begins. If your CIDP does not worsen during the wash-out, you will not continue to the treatment phase, and the study doctor will discuss your next treatment plan with you.

Whether this is the right study for you depends on how you and your doctor weigh this change against the potential benefit of participating. The study team discusses this in detail before you decide.

Who may be a good fit

A few headline criteria below. The screener checks the full eligibility list, and the study team confirms everything before enrollment.

Good fit

Adults 18 and older with confirmed CIDP

Diagnosed by a neurologist using 2021 international diagnostic criteria.

Currently on CIDP treatment

IVIG, SCIG, corticosteroids, or other standard maintenance therapy.

Condition stable for at least 12 weeks

No major symptom worsening or significant treatment dose changes.

Weakness in at least two limbs

INCAT disability score between 2 and 9 (if exactly 2, the weakness must be in your lower extremities).

Open to learning about the wash-out phase

Willing to have current treatment reduced and stopped for up to 12 weeks before the study medicine begins.

Able to understand and give informed consent

You understand the purpose and procedures of the study and are willing to participate.

Not eligible right now

Pure sensory or other CIDP variants

Certain CIDP variants are not part of this study's design.

High-dose IVIG or SCIG requirements

Currently needing more than 1.4 g/kg/month IVIG or 1.6 g/kg/month SCIG.

Prior failure to respond to IVIG/SCIG

If immunoglobulin therapy has not worked previously.

Recent immune-modulating therapies

Rituximab/alemtuzumab in past 12 months, efgartigimod in past 3 months, certain other agents.

Certain medical conditions

BMI over 35, chronic kidney disease, active hepatitis B/C or HIV, moderate-to-severe heart failure (NYHA III/IV), unstable heart conditions, a blood clot in the past 12 months, or a history of a blood-clotting disorder.

Pregnancy or contraception

Pregnant, breastfeeding, or unable to use reliable contraception during the study.

This study follows established clinical research and patient safety standards at every step.

Sponsored by Kedrion Biopharma

Kedrion Biopharma is a regulated biopharmaceutical company producing plasma-derived therapies, including IVIG, since 2001. In 2022 Kedrion combined with BPL (UK), adding 60+ years of immune globulin experience.

Registered and Regulated

Independent Ethics Review

An independent Institutional Review Board reviews this study to protect participant rights at every step.

Qualified Research Sites

Conducted at clinical research centers staffed by experienced neurologists and trained study coordinators familiar with CIDP care.

Voluntary Participation

Joining is voluntary. You may withdraw at any time, without penalty or affecting the medical care you would otherwise receive.

Frequently Asked Questions

The questions people ask us most, answered in plain language.

The KIg10 study is a Phase 3 clinical study testing a new IVIG (immune globulin) treatment for adults with CIDP. It is sponsored by Kedrion Biopharma and compares two doses to see how well each one works as ongoing treatment.

No placebo. Every participant receives an active KIg10. The study compares two doses (0.5 g/kg and 1.0 g/kg), randomly assigned. Neither you nor the doctor knows which dose you receive, but both are real, active medication.

Your current CIDP treatment is gradually reduced and stopped over up to 12 weeks before the study medicine begins. This is called the wash-out phase. The study team monitors you closely throughout. If your symptoms worsen, you move into the treatment phase and start KIg10. If they do not worsen, you will not continue, and the study doctor will discuss your next treatment plan with you.

KIg10 is an IVIG (immune globulin) treatment. The most common side effects are mild and happen during or shortly after the infusion: headache, fatigue, fever or chills, muscle aches, and nausea. These are usually managed by slowing the infusion, hydration, and pre-medications. The full safety profile is reviewed with you in detail before you join.

Yes. With your written permission, your regular neurologist is kept informed throughout the study. After the study ends, you return to your regular neurologist for ongoing care. You are not switching doctors.

Joining is voluntary. You may withdraw at any time, for any reason, without affecting your other medical care. If your CIDP symptoms worsen during the study, you receive a rescue dose of active KIg10 (2.0 g/kg). If you choose to leave the study, you return to your regular CIDP treatment with your neurologist.

If your answers suggest the study may be a fit, a registered nurse will call you to ask a few more questions and explain the study. If everything looks right and you agree, the nurse will refer you to the study site, where the study team makes the final decision about whether you can take part.

A Phase 3 clinical study investigating intravenous human immune globulin 10% (KIg10) as maintenance therapy for adults with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy. Sponsored by Kedrion Biopharma. Conducted under FDA-reviewed IND, ICH-GCP guidelines, and independent IRB oversight. Participation is voluntary.
